title: Pre-Algebra for a Junior High Student
audience: Junior high student taking pre-algebra for the first time

definition.what_is_pre_algebra: Pre-algebra is the math class that helps you move from basic arithmetic into algebra.
definition.main_idea: You begin using letters called variables to represent numbers you do not know yet.

topics.description: Number theory is about understanding different types of numbers and how they behave.
Factors are numbers that multiply together to create another number. Multiples are the results you get when multiplying a number by whole numbers.
Fractions, decimals, and percents are different ways of showing part of a whole.

addition_example.explanation: When the denominators are the same, add the numerators.

topics.description: A ratio compares two quantities. A proportion says that two ratios are equal.

proportion_example.meaning: Both fractions represent the same amount.

word_problem.question: If 3 notebooks cost $6, how much do 6 notebooks cost?

topics.description: Variables are letters that represent numbers. Expressions contain numbers, variables, and operations. Equations contain an equals sign.
topics.important_rule: Whatever you do to one side of an equation, you must also do to the other side.

topics.description: An exponent tells you how many times to multiply a number by itself. A square root asks what number multiplied by itself creates another number.
Pre-algebra introduces formulas for finding things like area, perimeter, and missing sides.

pre_algebra.description: Pre-algebra teaches the basic rules and skills needed before algebra.

algebra.description: Algebra uses the same ideas in more complicated equations.

pre_algebra_vs_algebra.main_difference: Pre-algebra introduces variables, equations, formulas, and number rules. Algebra uses those skills to solve more complicated problems.

hypotenuse.question: A right triangle has sides 6 and 8. Find the hypotenuse.

key_vocabulary.variable: A letter that represents a number.
key_vocabulary.expression: A math statement with numbers, variables, and operations but no equals sign.
key_vocabulary.equation: A math statement showing that two expressions are equal.
key_vocabulary.coefficient: A number multiplied by a variable, such as 3 in 3x.
key_vocabulary.constant: A number without a variable, such as 5 in 2x + 5.
key_vocabulary.factor: A number that divides evenly into another number.
key_vocabulary.multiple: The result of multiplying a number by a whole number.
key_vocabulary.exponent: A number that tells how many times the base is multiplied by itself.
key_vocabulary.square_root: A number that, when multiplied by itself, gives the original number.
key_vocabulary.hypotenuse: The longest side of a right triangle.

main_takeaway: Pre-algebra is mostly about learning how numbers, variables, equations, and formulas work together. If you understand substitution, order of operations, fractions, negative numbers, and how to solve simple equations, you will have a strong foundation for algebra.
